findings.title: Redeploying POSTs every existing secret again, which probably fails on duplicate names.
findings.body: In the update phase, the code deletes only the secrets that were removed, then calls `insertSecrets` with every secret, including ones that already exist. That calls the create endpoint (`POST .../secrets`) for names already in the store. A normal redeploy with unchanged secrets will likely fail with a duplicate-name error, and changed values are never updated through the PATCH endpoint. Adopting a store that already holds those secrets (line 239) hits the same problem. The existing test only passes because it renames every secret. Fix: compare against `listSecrets`, create only new names, and update existing ones through the per-secret edit endpoint.

findings.title: Secrets Store binding metadata has the wrong type and binds a secret that doesn't exist.
findings.body: Cloudflare binds Secrets Store secrets one at a time, with type `secrets_store_secret`, a `store_id` and the name of one secret in that store. This code sends `type: "secrets_store"` and sets `secret_name` to the binding name (for example `SECRETS`), which is not a secret in the store. Deploying a Worker with `bindings: { SECRETS: store }` will either be rejected by the script upload API or bind a missing secret. Fix: use `secrets_store_secret` and require the caller to name the secret, either with a per-secret binding object or by expanding `store.secrets` into one binding per secret. The `WorkerBindingSecretsStore` type in bindings.ts has the same wrong `type` literal.

findings.title: Changing `name` on update is silently ignored.
findings.body: In the update phase, the code never compares `props.name` with `this.output.name`. It keeps the old store but returns the new `name` in state, so the state no longer matches the real store in Cloudflare. Fix: when the name changes, replace or recreate the store, or throw an error.

findings.title: Secrets Store bindings are silently left out of wrangler.json.
findings.body: The comment says these bindings go into a `secrets_store_secrets` array, but the branch does nothing and no such array is written. Generated wrangler.json, local dev and type generation will be missing the binding. Fix: push `{binding, store_id, secret_name}` entries into `spec.secrets_store_secrets`.

findings.title: Unrelated change to the shared test helper drops the describe-block prefix from scope names.
findings.body: Before this change, each test scope was named `<describe>/<test>`; now it is just the test name. Tests with the same name in different `describe` blocks of the same file now share a scope and state, so their resources can collide or be destroyed by each other. The issue doesn't ask for this. Fix: revert this hunk.

findings.title: Assertion compares the ID with itself, so it can never fail.
findings.body: `expect(secretsStore.id).toEqual(secretsStore.id)` passes even if the update created a different store. Save the first ID and compare the updated store's ID against it.

findings.title: The runtime type promises a store-level `get(secretName)` that Workers don't provide.
findings.body: A Secrets Store binding in a Worker is a single secret whose `get()` takes no arguments. Typing it as `get(secretName: keyof S)` lets user code like `env.SECRETS.get("API_KEY")` type-check even though it does not do what the type says at runtime. Fix: model the binding as one secret with `get(): Promise<string>` and bind each secret separately.

findings.title: Secrets are created with empty `scopes`, so Workers can't read them.
findings.body: Cloudflare uses `scopes` to decide which services may use a secret (for example `["workers"]`). With `scopes: []`, the secrets this resource creates are not usable from a Worker binding, which is the main thing the issue asks for. Fix: default to `["workers"]` or make scopes configurable.

held.title: Calling `bind()` during deploy may throw or return undefined.
held.body: `SecretsStore()` calls `bind(store)` and reads `binding.get` while running in the deploy/provisioning process, not inside a Worker. If `bind` throws or returns undefined outside the Worker runtime, every `SecretsStore(...)` call fails. I could not check `runtime/bind.ts` from here. Fix: return the resource directly, as other Cloudflare resources do.

held.title: Bulk delete probably sends secret names where the API expects secret IDs.
held.body: `listSecrets` returns only names, and `deleteSecrets` sends that array of names as the body of the bulk DELETE. Cloudflare's bulk-delete endpoint takes secret IDs. If so, removing a secret from `props.secrets` will either fail or leave the secret in place. I could not confirm the exact API contract from here. Fix: have `listSecrets` return `{id, name}` and delete by ID. `listSecrets` and `findSecretsStoreByName` also read only the first page of results.
